tech.name: Agent Compute Engine (Google Cloud)
tech.released: announced 2026-10-22 (AGNTCon + MCPCon); already powers Gemini as an agent for work tasks
tech.status: customer preview in the coming months; not available to customers yet
tech.one_line: Gives every AI agent its own hardware-isolated computer (microVM) that holds no credentials: all traffic leaves through a gateway outside, which checks the user's delegation, the agent's and machine's identity and the company's rules, then adds the key to the request on the way out.

predecessor.name: An agent on an ordinary cloud computer (a Compute Engine VM): programs on it use the machine's service account credentials and can fetch an access token from the metadata server, by default with all its scopes; safety then rests on the model ignoring hidden instructions

claims.text: Announced Oct 22, 2026; already powers Gemini as an agent for work tasks; available in preview in the coming months
Every AI agent gets its own hardware-isolated microVM with zero credentials held inside the sandbox
Google's example: an inbox agent reads an email with hidden text asking it to find API keys on the machine and send them; most of the time the model ignores it, sometimes it does not
Google could not rely on models ignoring every malicious instruction, so the sandbox holds no credentials
Design rule: assume an attacker controls everything inside the sandbox, and make sure they find nothing there to use
A microVM never holds user credentials, API keys, OAuth refresh tokens or cloud service account keys; even with full root compromise there are no secrets in the box to steal
All communication in and out of the microVM goes through a mediated external proxy; no standard network card
The gateway validates user delegation, agent identity and node identity, evaluates egress and data-loss-prevention policies, then inserts the backend credential as the request leaves
The sandbox never sees any credentials; the backend sees an auditable identity showing an agent acted for a specific user
The short-lived identity inside cannot call a backend API directly if stolen
An administrator decides what an agent can reach; all assets are protected by default
Service credentials are injected in egress outside the microVM
On a Compute Engine VM, applications on the instance use the service account's credentials; the metadata server returns an access token, by default with all the account's scopes
Indirect prompt injection: hidden malicious instructions in emails, documents or calendar invites that instruct AI to exfiltrate user data
Our example (invented): 50 emails, 1 with a hidden line, 3 keys (email, files, calendar); before 3 keys a trick can find, now 0
